transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As we all know, the family wants to preserve several older relatives' stories in recordings for future family members, and I've got the only working camcorder. I'm coordinating the recording evening and will be deciding how the files are handled afterward. We'll be capturing both video and spoken audio, and we have the shared family digital drive available. Before I finalize the plan, I want to hear from each of you individually. Nina, could you go first? Please share any preferences, advice, or constraints you have about the recording or file handling. Then Omar, I'll ask you the same.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I want to share something important my grandmother told me. She is willing to be recorded for the family archive, but only on the condition that the interviews are never posted publicly online. They should stay within the family archive on the shared drive and not be shared outside the family or on any public platforms. I think we need to build this constraint into our file-handling plan.

transcript.text: Before we finalize the plan, I want to share some advice I got from my friend Priya, who works as an audiovisual archivist. She recommended that the audio should be captured as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and that we should make two verified backup copies. I think we should build these specifications into our recording and file-handling plan to make sure these stories are preserved properly for future family members.
